question: The science club has 25 members: 10 boys and 15 girls.  A 5-person committee is chosen at random.  What is the probability that the committee has at least 1 boy and at least 1 girl?
solution:
There are $\binom{25}{5}=53{,}130$ equally likely committees. A committee fails the condition only if all five members are boys or all five are girls. These cases are disjoint, with $\binom{10}{5}=252$ and $\binom{15}{5}=3{,}003$ committees, respectively. Thus the desired probability is $\frac{53{,}130-252-3{,}003}{53{,}130}=\frac{49{,}875}{53{,}130}=\frac{475}{506}$, dividing numerator and denominator by 105.
Final answer: \dfrac{475}{506}
